chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about praying in the mosque of Ghadir Khumm during the day while I am a traveler, so he said: 'Pray in it, for there is virtue in it, and my father used to command that.'

key_terms.غَدِيرِ خُمٍّ: Ghadir Khumm, a location near Mecca associated with the event of Ghadir and possessing spiritual virtue
key_terms.مُسَافِرٌ: Traveler (one on a journey, eligible for shortened prayers)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for praying in the mosque of Ghadir Khumm while traveling?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the specific virtue of Ghadir Khumm as a place of prayer, linking the authority of Imam al-Sadiq directly to his father, Imam al-Baqir, thereby reinforcing the continuity of religious practice within the Ahl al-Bayt. It highlights the Shia emphasis on visiting and praying in sites associated with key events of the Imams' lives, treating them as loci of spiritual merit (fadl) rather than merely historical markers.
